subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Caissons: Building Underwater Foundations
description: A fast breakdown of Caissons: Building Underwater Foundations for builders.

hook.text: Bridge piers in rivers need foundations on the riverbed. Workers used to dig them inside air-pressurized chambers.

buildup.text: A caisson is a watertight box sunk to the riverbed. Workers inside dig out soil while the box sinks under its own weight.

discovery.text: Compressed air keeps water out. Workers entered through airlocks — like tiny submarines underground.

twist.text: Workers surfacing too fast got caisson disease — the bends. The Brooklyn Bridge killed over 20 workers this way.

climax.text: Modern drilled shafts and cofferdams have mostly replaced manned caissons. Machines now do the dangerous work.

punchline.text: Sink a box. Dig out the bottom. Build on bedrock.

quiz.question: What caused caisson disease among Brooklyn Bridge workers?
options: Toxic gases released from river mud during excavation
Surfacing too fast from pressurized chambers caused the bends
Prolonged exposure to cold water weakened their immune systems
